articles.title: After nearly 500 years without beavers around Loch Ness, Scottish conservation groups have won approval to reintroduce up to 15 family groups over three years; the first releases are expected within weeks
articles.summary: Wild beavers are set to return to the Loch Ness catchment area for the first time in 500 years after officials approved a major rewilding project in the
articles.body: Wild beavers are set to return to the Loch Ness catchment area for the first time in 500 years after officials approved a major rewilding project in the Scottish Highlands. Scottish nature agency NatureScot has granted an official release licence to conservation charities Trees for Life and the Beaver Trust. Under the approved Ness Beaver Project, conservation teams will release up to 15 beaver family groups into suitable waterways across the River Ness catchment over three years. The first releases could begin within weeks, marking an important moment for wildlife and nature in the Scottish Highlands.Official approval opens door for Highland releaseNatureScot approved the releases after carrying out detailed environmental checks and consulting local landowners, farmers and Highland communities. The agency identified the Loch Ness catchment in 2022 as one of Scotland's most suitable places for beavers because of its large network of waterways that can support the animals, according to Trees for Life. All beavers chosen for the project will undergo strict health checks before being moved to their new homes. The first stage will focus on selected locations that are suitable for wildlife between Fort Augustus and Lochend. Jenny Bryce, beaver team manager at NatureScot, said: "Bringing beavers back to this beautiful place will be great progress for Scotland's Beaver Strategy, bringing benefits for nature, climate and people." She added: "We have assessed the monitoring and mitigation plans set out by the applicants and believe that, along with our existing Beaver Mitigation Scheme, any potential conflicts that may arise can be resolved."Reversing five centuries of absenceEurasian beavers were hunted to extinction in Scotland during the 16th century. Heavy hunting for their fur, meat and castoreum, a substance used in perfumes, was the main reason for their disappearance. Their loss changed local rivers and waterways. Without beavers, natural wetlands were no longer maintained in the same way. These wetland areas had supported native fish, birds and water plants for thousands of years. The planned releases at Loch Ness are part of Scotland's wider beaver strategy. The plan aims to bring the native animals back to suitable river catchments across the country. Beavers became a protected species in Scotland in 2019. This means approved relocation can be used to manage their populations instead of killing them. The return of these water-loving animals is expected to help create natural wetlands, improve water quality and slow the flow of rainwater into rivers. Their activities could also provide new habitats for many insects, amphibians and bird species across the Great Glen.Managing land use and local concernsProject organisers understand that beaver activities, such as building dams and cutting down trees, can sometimes cause problems for farming and forestry. For this reason, the project teams spoke with local communities before receiving official approval. Trees for Life has appointed dedicated beaver management officers to work with local farmers and property owners. Under NatureScot's support scheme, landowners will be able to get help with problems caused by beavers. This includes protective wraps for trees, devices to control water flow and free expert advice to deal with local flooding or damage to timber. Field teams are now completing transport plans and preparing the release sites. The first beaver families are expected to be released before the end of the year. For a closer look at how beavers can change Scottish rivers and their surrounding habitats, viewers can watch an overview of Scotland's Beaver Reintroduction Impact. articles.title: ‘Please help us’: Savannah Guthrie issues new plea for help in mother’s kidnapping
articles.summary: Heartbroken “TODAY” co-host Savannah Guthrie on Sunday renewed her plea for information about the kidnapping of her 84-year-old mother, Nancy Guthrie, from her Tucson, Arizona, home nine months ago.
articles.body: Heartbroken “TODAY” co-host Savannah Guthrie on Sunday renewed her plea for information about the kidnapping of her 84-year-old mother, Nancy Guthrie, from her Tucson, Arizona, home nine months ago. Guthrie posted an image on Instagram of a drawing by her young daughter that evoked her feelings about her elderly mother’s disappearance. The drawing shows a blue umbrella surrounded by raindrops, with a caption that reads: “I know it might not seem like it but I really need my mommy.” Her child’s artwork “says so much about how I feel,” Guthrie wrote. “For Annie and Tommy, for Cam and Kristine, for Mike and me and for all of mom’s beloved grandchildren: we ache for her, we cry out for answers, we cannot move forward,” Guthrie said in the post, naming members of her immediate family. “We need someone to help us, tell us what you know.” Nancy Guthrie was reported missing from her Tucson home on Feb. 1. Authorities have said the crime involved a ransom demand. The investigation by the Pima County Sheriff’s Department, with assistance from the FBI, has not produced any significant breaks in the case. A hair found in Nancy Guthrie’s home did not lead to a suspect after testing, investigators said in July. A task force created to solve the crime is still chasing leads in an effort to find Nancy Guthrie and any suspect involved. The team “traveled to Florida to meet with lab scientists to see what more could be done to advance the case,” the sheriff’s office recently said on X. Guthrie said her family has been changed forever by the tragedy. She called her mother “a light in this world” and begged for answers so her family can “celebrate her and give her the dignity she deserves.” The morning show host noted that the reward for information is still available. “We are begging you,” Guthrie wrote. “Please help us.”

articles.title: At risk Cumbrian in-person postpartum mums' groups saved
articles.summary: The Happy Mums Foundation supports women experiencing postpartum mental health challenges.
articles.body:
A mothers' support service has said it is "absolutely thrilled" after it received £70,000 worth of grants to maintain its in-person wellbeing groups.

The Happy Mums Foundation, which supports women experiencing postpartum mental health challenges, was set up in 2015 and has helped more than 1,000 families across Cumbria.

Last month the organisation said its in-person peer support groups were at risk due to funding pressures.

But grants from both the Postcode and National Lottery mean that the immediate risk has been lifted, said director Lucinda Bray. "We can keep supporting mums," she said.

Due to funding pressures, the organisation had been considering moving its in-person peer support groups online.

But Bray previously told the BBC that the loss of these real world safe spaces could worsen the mental health of vulnerable women in the county.

She said that being able to talk about suicidal thinking was actually "quite a good preventative factor".

"If that doesn't have an outlet and you don't have a safe space to talk about those things, where might they go?" she said.

The foundation has since been awarded £50,000 by the Postcode Lottery and £20,000 from the National Lottery.

"It means that we can continue the groups we are running and we can continue working on ways to make our organisation more sustainable for the future."

articles.summary: A British treasury minister has reignited a political row over Labour’s definition of “working people” after saying employers do not fall under the
articles.body: A British treasury minister has reignited a political row over Labour’s definition of “working people” after saying employers do not fall under the category, drawing criticism from opposition politicians who accused the government of overlooking the contribution of small-business owners.Chief secretary to the treasury Emma Reynolds made the remarks during an interview with GB News on Sunday. Asked about people affected by Labour’s economic policies, Reynolds said: “I don’t think employers are working people, they are companies.”When host Camilla Tominey asked whether that meant she was not a working person because she employed a cleaner, Reynolds replied: “No, but you’re an employee probably of your company, and I’m saying there is a difference between employers and employees.”The comments prompted a backlash from Conservative politicians. Shadow business minister Bradley Thomas accused Labour of displaying a “patronising, out-of-touch” attitude towards small businesses, pointing to electricians who take on apprentices and shop owners who employ young people for weekend work.Shadow work and pensions minister Helen Whately said the remarks showed that Labour did not understand that businesses were built through hard work. Shadow defence secretary James Cartlidge also criticised the distinction, saying employing people was among the hardest parts of running a business.The exchange has revived scrutiny of Labour’s 2024 manifesto pledge not to raise taxes on “working people”, including income tax, national insurance and VAT. The pledge became contentious after former chancellor Rachel Reeves raised employers’ national insurance contributions in October 2024.The government argued that the increase did not breach the commitment because it applied to employers rather than employees. The main rate of employers’ national insurance rose from 13.5% to 15%, while the secondary threshold — the level above which employers begin paying the contribution — was reduced from £9,100 to £5,000.A Treasury spokesperson defended the government’s position, saying it would stick to its manifesto commitments and would not increase the rates of income tax, employee national insurance, VAT or corporation tax.You use AI every day. articles.title: California doctor defrauded Medicare of more than $45 million through fake Botox claims; spent the money on five properties, two Teslas and expensive collectibles; sentenced to 15 years in federal prison
articles.summary: A California doctor who defrauded Medicare of more than $45 million by billing for Botox injections she never administered has been sentenced to 15 years
articles.body: A California doctor who defrauded Medicare of more than $45 million by billing for Botox injections she never administered has been sentenced to 15 years in federal prison. Violetta Mailyan, 45, used the proceeds of the elaborate healthcare fraud scheme to purchase multimillion-dollar properties, luxury cars and expensive collectibles, according to the US Department of Justice (DOJ).Mailyan, who operated the Healthy Way Medical Center clinic in Glendale, California, was convicted in May by a federal jury in the Central District of California on nine counts of wire fraud and three counts of obstruction of a criminal investigation into a healthcare offence. Her sentence was announced by the DOJ on Friday.In addition to the prison term, Mailyan has been ordered to forfeit more than $16 million in assets and pay approximately $32.9 million in restitution to Medicare.Doctor billed Medicare for Botox injections she never administeredAccording to prosecutors, Mailyan fraudulently billed Medicare for thousands of Botox injections that were either never administered or were not provided for the approved medical purpose of treating chronic migraines.Medicare reimburses healthcare providers for Botox injections when they are required to treat documented cases of chronic migraines. However, investigators found that Mailyan submitted claims for treatments that had not taken place.Prosecutors said she also billed Medicare for more than $19 million in injections supposedly administered on days when her clinic was closed. On several other occasions, she submitted claims while travelling outside California, including during trips to Mexico, Hawaii, Las Vegas, Pennsylvania and New York.In one particularly striking example, Mailyan allegedly billed more than $200,000 for treatments supposedly provided to patients in California while she was actually vacationing in Cabo, Mexico.A photograph recovered from her phone and presented by prosecutors showed a scenic beach view in Cabo on a day she had billed Medicare $34,560 for services allegedly provided at her Glendale clinic.Forged medical records and signatures to conceal fraudThe investigation also revealed that Mailyan attempted to cover up the fraudulent billing by falsifying medical records after investigators began examining her activities.Prosecutors said she forged the signatures of Medicare beneficiaries, including one man who was in prison during the period when she claimed to have treated him.She also submitted the fabricated records to federal investigators after receiving a grand jury subpoena seeking medical documentation. According to prosecutors, the records were intended to make it appear that she had provided treatments to patients she had never seen.The scale of her billing activity reportedly made her an extreme outlier among doctors receiving Medicare payments for Botox treatments. Prosecutors said Mailyan received six times the amount paid to the next-highest group of providers, which consisted entirely of neurologists.Bought five properties, two Teslas and expensive collectiblesAuthorities said Mailyan used the proceeds of the Medicare fraud to fund an extravagant lifestyle. She purchased five pieces of California real estate, including properties in Surfside and Glendale.The DOJ had previously said that four of her properties had combined equity of approximately $7.3 million. She also purchased two Tesla vehicles, one of them a Cybertruck.Her spending extended to rare and expensive collectibles. Among the items she acquired were a 17th-century crossbow valued at approximately $12,000 and a painting of Ludwig I, Crown Prince of Bavaria, worth around $3,000.As part of the sentence, Mailyan was ordered to forfeit more than $16 million in property, including bank funds, personal belongings, real estate and securities. She must also pay approximately $32.9 million in restitution to Medicare.It was not immediately clear when she would begin serving her prison sentence.Trump administration steps up efforts to tackle government fraudThe case comes amid the Trump administration's wider efforts to crack down on fraud involving government programmes. President Donald Trump established a task force to eliminate fraud in March and placed Vice President JD Vance in charge of the initiative.The DOJ has said its work to combat fraud supports the administration's efforts. In October, Trump also announced a $25 million programme aimed at encouraging members of the public to report suspected government fraud.Under the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program, individuals whose tips lead to a fraud conviction or significant federal enforcement action could receive up to $30,000. The Justice Department will administer the programme.During the announcement, Trump said the reward could amount to a one per cent commission on the amount of fraud uncovered through a tip. He also said he would decide who received the money if multiple people claimed responsibility for providing the information.Meanwhile, Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Dr Mehmet Oz has raised concerns about possible organised fraud involving senior care centres. In October, Oz alleged that the Chinese mafia could be orchestrating Medicaid fraud through such facilities.During visits to Kent Senior Care and Evergreen Adult Day Care in Flushing, Queens, Oz described the experience as suspicious and suggested that organised groups could be facilitating fraudulent claims. His remarks came as part of a multi-agency federal investigation.New York Governor Kathy Hochul, meanwhile, has said the state is undertaking a major effort to combat Medicaid fraud and abuse.Trump has also announced that more than 20 million seniors would receive unexpected Medicare payments of $90. The payments are intended to help eligible Medicare Part B beneficiaries cover their premiums.The President claimed that the money represented surplus funds collected through fees used to operate HealthCare.gov during the Biden administration. In a letter accompanying the announcement, Trump said the money belonged to working Americans and was being returned to them, CBS News reported.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 5 US destinations named to Best of World travel list for 2027 by National Geographic
articles.summary: Madison, Wisconsin, leads National Geographic's 2027 Best of the World list, with four other U.S. destinations selected. Choices span from California to Maryland.
articles.body: Five locations in the U.S. have been chosen by National Geographic as some of the best to travel to in the year ahead. National Geographic’s annual Best of the World travel list, just released, features 25 travel-worthy destinations all over the globe. The five standout U.S. destinations harbor stunning views, great food and unique cultural spaces. AMERICANS CHOOSING TO VISIT SMALLER TOWNS OVER BIG CITIES AS TRAVEL COSTS RISE Check out the details. 1. Madison, Wisconsin This capital city was listed as the first U.S.-based destination to visit, highlighted for its lakefront adventure opportunities and local cuisine. Nestled between Lakes Mendota and Monona, Madison, Wisconsin, offers beautiful trails and green spaces. It's also city-central for several colleges, including the University of Wisconsin-Madison. This mix between college town, nature oasis and state capital gives Madison a unique flare, pairing beloved nightlife spaces with a growing trail network. National Geographic calls the city of about 290,000 residents "compact enough to explore on foot or by bike," as it’s certified by the League of American Bicyclists. NY AND LA DIDN'T WIN AMERICA'S BEST MEGA AIRPORT TITLE, BUT ONE MIDWEST HUB DID Madison reportedly is home to more than 200 miles of hiking trails and bikeways. These connect neighborhoods, beaches and about 300 parks, which, according to National Geographic, is among the most per capita of any U.S. city. Bikers can take the 13-mile bike loop around Lake Monona, which passes from the Olbrich Botanical Gardens to Madison’s downtown waterfront. The Dane County Farmers Market takes place on Saturdays in the summer on Capitol Square, with up to 20,000 visitors. It is reportedly the nation’s largest producer-only market, providing flowers, baked goods and fresh vegetables. 4 US HOTSPOTS JUST MADE NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC'S TOP TRAVEL LIST National Geographic also shouted out some local restaurants, such as Fairchild for its use of local vegetables in homemade ravioli and Ahan for its classic Laotian dishes. 2. Pacific Coast Highway, California After mudslides in Big Sur caused a three-year closure, some of the most scenic sections of the Pacific Coast Highway have been reopened, giving travelers the opportunity to take in the inspirational sights of California’s coastline. "Lesser known artsy communities" lie just outside the roadway, says National Geographic. On the southern end, artist colony Laguna Beach celebrates its centennial in 2027. Downtown Laguna Beach not only offers beach access, but fronts a new pedestrian promenade with boutiques, galleries, outdoor performance spaces and "al fresco" dining. The central-coast city of Lompoc features a trail of more than 30 murals depicting the town’s agricultural roots, as well as a wine region known as the Wine Ghetto. North of Lompoc is the one-block dairy farmer town of Harmony, which boasts a population of 18. The town features small-batch ice cream at Harmony Valley Creamery, and other locally owned businesses like Harmony Glassworks and Harmony Pottery Studio and Gallery. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The northern end of the highway is home to more artistic regions, like Mendocino County and Fort Bragg, offering exhibitions and galleries like Pacific Textile Arts. 3. Southern Ozarks, Missouri and Arkansas In the heart of the United States, spanning between Missouri and Arkansas, the southern Ozarks show off "spectacular" bluffs, valleys and ridgelines. The region is a "haven" for outdoor activities, National Geographic said, as well as immerse cultural activities in neighboring towns like Bentonville, Arkansas — home to the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art. Close to Bentonville, Bella Vista, Arkansas, is the self-proclaimed mountain biking capital of the world, fronting the new OZ Trails Bike Park. It's the state’s first chairlift-served mountain bike park for access to 20 miles of trails for all levels. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES About 60 miles across the Missouri border is Dogwood Canyon Nature Park, where the Ozarks unfold across 10,000 acres, featuring limestone cliffs and valleys, National Geographic detailed. Herds of elk, bison and longhorn cattle can be spotted here. Visitors can hike and bike the park’s network of trails. 4. Baltimore, Maryland Baltimore is packed with U.S. history as the birthplace of the American railroad. The port city on the shores of the Chesapeake Bay chartered the country’s first commercial railroad in 1827. The National Museum of Railroad History & Innovation will reportedly mark the 200-year anniversary with a $38 million upgrade. The museum’s makeover will feature "archival treasures" like letters from Abraham Lincoln and railroad tech exhibits, according to NatGeo. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER National Geographic also highlighted Baltimore’s historic Lexington Market, established in 1782. The public market features merchants like family-owned seafood, produce and baked goods vendors. Baltimore’s Inner Harbor has attractions like the National Aquarium and 1854 U.S.S. Constellation warship, as well as parks and retail stores. The waterfront features a whiskey distillery, green spaces and restaurants offering local delicacy options, like steamed crabs and crab cakes. The Baltimore Blueway has launched kayaking trails, National Geographic reported. A trip to Fort McHenry also came as a recommendation, as it's the location that inspired Francis Scott Key to write "The Star-Spangled Banner." 5. Catalina Island National Geographic called attention to a second California location, Catalina Island — a remote destination only accessible by boat. An hour on the ferry from Long Beach, California, brings visitors to the island's sweeping landscape, including ridgelines and roving bison. Catalina Island is also home to indigenous plant and animal species, like small foxes that can be spotted along the 38.5 mile Trans-Catalina Trail, and coastal sage shrub. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Garden to Sky Trail offers an ocean overlook from the Wrigley Memorial and Botanic Garden, which showcases "rare island flora," National Geographic said.

articles.title: US calls Turkey-Libya maritime deal 'unhelpful and provocative' amid regional backlash
articles.summary: A State Department spokesperson called the Turkey-Libya maritime accord "unhelpful and provocative" as diplomatic tensions escalate in the region.
articles.body: The Trump State Department denounced the recent eastern Mediterranean maritime agreement between NATO member Turkey and the fractured Libyan state. The Turkey-Libya deal has also caused frustration and anger among many nations because they say it rewrote the established sea borders of the sensitive Mediterranean Sea region, where large deposits of gas might be located. The Eastern Libyan parliament approved the maritime accord in mid-October. The region is ruled by military leader Khalifa Haftar, who has formed an alliance with Turkey — the maritime deal ignores Libya’s internationally recognized government in Tripoli in the northwestern part of the oil-rich country. A U.S. State Department spokesperson told Fox News Digital: "The announcement of the ratification of the Turkish-Libyan delimitation memorandum of understanding has raised tensions in the region and is unhelpful and provocative — and our position on this matter has not changed." BILLION-DOLLAR POWER LINK CONNECTING ISRAEL TO EUROPE HITS ROADBLOCK IN BITTER REGIONAL FEUD The spokesperson added: "We encourage all countries, including partners in the Eastern Mediterranean, to resolve maritime disputes through good-faith negotiations and avoid any provocative behavior. Greece and Türkiye are both NATO allies. We encourage them to engage bilaterally to address any areas of disagreement." According to the spokesperson, "Peaceful resolution of such disputes opens the way for commercial investment and exploration that will benefit the entire region." According to the Turkish news agency Anadolu Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Wednesday said the maritime agreement between Turkey and Libya was "entirely legitimate" and not in violation of international law. He added: "This is an entirely legitimate agreement, both from a legal and a political perspective. There is no need to debate it." Reuters reported Fidan also shot back at critics of the deal. "There are countries reacting to this. We know why they are reacting. Some are doing so because they need to, some really do have strategic problems with this issue. ​ However, this is an entirely legitimate deal, both from a legal and a statutory perspective. ​There is no need to argue this." NETANYAHU WARNS TURKEY SHOULD NOT GET F-35S, CITING ERDOĞAN'S HOSTILITY TOWARD NATO ALLIES Fox News Digital sought comment from both Turkey and Libya but did not get a response by time of publication. Greek Minister of Foreign Affairs George Gerapetritis angrily wrote on his ministry’s website that, "The memorandum will not be implemented. And it will not be implemented for the simple reason that it produces no legal effects whatsoever, as it is entirely contrary to international law." He added, "Türkiye had established a system of influence in Libya, essentially seeking to advance its own interests" and the Turkish media has ramped up its anti-Greece rhetoric. "There is a constant stream of reports pushing the Turkish government to become even more aggressive." Endy Zemenides, the executive director of the Hellenic American Leadership Council, told Fox News Digital that the Turkey-Libya agreement "absolutely" endangers the security of the U.S. and its allies. He said: "This memorandum specifically infringes on U.S. companies and U.S. energy policy. It effectively denies maritime rights and zones of Crete. Crete is NATO’s southernmost base. And the U.S. has been increasingly relied upon because of wars in the Mideast." He noted that the American companies Exxon and Chevron are present in Crete. US-BACKED ISRAEL-MOROCCO DEAL DEEPENS ABRAHAM ACCORDS AMID GROWING REGIONAL THREATS Zemenides said the Turkey-Libya deal is a way of pushing the U.S. out of the region. The U.S. has not been able to rely on Turkey for a decade, said Zemenides. He continued that "allowing Turkey to challenge the pro-Western order" is not good for American interests. The European Union invoked unusually strong language targeting the deal, declaring it in violation of maritime law. "The EU position regarding the MoU is firm and clear. As outlined in the European Council Conclusions of December 2019 and reiterated in June 2025, the Türkiye-Libya Memorandum of Understanding infringes upon the sovereign rights of third States and does not comply with the Law of the Sea. It is null and void and cannot produce any legal consequences for third States." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Israel also blasted Turkey and Libya. The Jewish state has developed a troika alliance with both Greece and Cyprus. Israel’s foreign ministry said on X it "strongly condemns the decision of the Libyan House of Representatives to ratify the Maritime Jurisdiction Memorandum between Turkey and Libya." Israel’s foreign ministry added on X, "This agreement infringes upon the sovereign rights of our close allies in the region. Regretfully, once again we see Turkey working to destabilize the east Mediterranean region." Reuters contributed to this report.

articles.title: Russia arrests minor after US tip-off on terror plot targeting Moscow
articles.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has detained a minor suspected of planning a terrorist attack at a popular museum and park complex in Moscow,
articles.body: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has detained a minor suspected of planning a terrorist attack at a popular museum and park complex in Moscow, following a tip-off from the United States about an imminent mass-casualty threat.The FSB said on Sunday that it had received information from US counterparts through established partner channels about preparations for an attack at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve in southern Moscow. The security agency said the information had prompted it to take appropriate measures and that a suspect had subsequently been detained.According to Russian news agency Interfax, the minor had posted photographs on TikTok showing himself wearing tactical clothing and a balaclava while holding an object resembling an automatic weapon. He had also shared photographs taken at the Tsaritsyno estate with the caption: "I found a place."Searches of the suspect's home reportedly led investigators to recover the clothing and accessories seen in the social media posts. His mobile phone also contained a subscription to a neo-Nazi channel on Telegram, along with what the FSB described as "a significant number of searches concerning terrorist attacks, mass killings and other acts of violence".Russia's Investigative Committee is considering further legal and procedural action against the minor, the FSB said.The detention came a day after the US Embassy in Moscow issued an urgent security alert, warning of a "credible threat of a mass casualty event" at the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve on October 31. The embassy said the US government was coordinating with Russian authorities over the response and advised American citizens to avoid the location and large crowds.The warning triggered a security operation at the historic estate, with Russian authorities temporarily closing the complex and evacuating visitors and staff. The site was shut on Saturday, with officials initially citing "technical reasons".Security personnel were deployed around the former imperial estate as emergency measures were put in place. Musician Lilia Pechenkina, who was performing at the reserve when the alert was triggered, said evacuation sirens sounded over the public address system as she was finishing her performance.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gavin and Stacey's Neil the Baby hopes to be next Stereophonics
articles.summary: Oscar Hartland, who played Neil the Baby, says he's on a "mission to create a new modern sound for Wales".
articles.body:
Gavin and Stacey fans will likely remember Oscar Hartland, or Neil the Baby, for his heart-warming performance of The Beatle's Blackbird in the sitcom's 2024 finale.

The episode was watched by about 12.3m people on Christmas day and saw Hartland's character serenade the crowd at the wedding of his on-screen dad Smithy, played by James Cordon.

But that was just the start for Hartland, now 17, who says his band is aiming to be "the next 'Phonics, or something like that".

He has recently released a new single and he and his fellow band members are on a "mission to create a new modern sound for Wales".

Hartland, from Machen, Caerphilly county, said his latest release, Wild Bull, was rooted in "being a bit crazy" and the challenges of growing up in the south Wales valleys.

The actor and singer went on his first tour in 2025 and said the past few months had been about "figuring out the earth behind the sound" with his bandmates Cayden Hughes on bass, Aiden Williams on drums, and Deacon Ball on electric guitar.

"We've had lots of people say it's rocky, but it's Welsh and it's got lots of stuff behind it," he told Lucy Owen on BBC Radio Wales .

"Growing up, I was just a wild bull, I was just mental, you know, in school, just out and about, playing rugby, being wild, being crazy. I know loads of my friends who are just the same.

"It's very hard as a young lad, especially Wales in the valleys, to keep yourself contained, because there is so much trouble to get up to."

Hartland said he surrounded himself with music growing up and described himself as a bit of a "black sheep".

"I was playing the piano while everyone else was watching rugby," he said.

But he added the new single was all about "letting go and saying, 'this is me I'm a wild bull'."

Hartland said the response to the song, which was released on Friday, had been brilliant.

"People are loving it, the interaction is nuts... it's really nice.

"The biggest thing is trying to create a movement, that people can feel a part of."

At 14 years old, Hartland took part in The Voice Kids in the hopes of kickstarting his rock career.

His performance of Foo Fighters' My Hero impressed the judges and was also seen by Gavin and Stacey writers James Cordon and Ruth Jones, who approached him with the idea of performing in the series finale.

The Christmas day finale episode became one of the most watched scripted TV shows of the century , seen by 19.11 million people after seven days of catch-up viewing and beating the show's previous record of 17.92m for the 2019 Christmas special.

Nearly two years on, Hartland said it "blows his mind" that people are still talking about it.

Hartland added support was "always there" from his fellow Gavin and Stacey cast members, which was "lush".

"A lot of people don't really know what it would be like to be in our boots, I suppose, sort of, with the size of it," he said.

He said it was nice to see cast members pursuing "other adventures" too, such as Melanie Walters, who played Gwen, recently taking part in Strictly Come Dancing .

Hartland has been recording at Rockfield studios in Monmouth, which has also played host to the likes of Oasis, Iggy Pop and Queen.

"I want to record there all the time, because I just love what the place is about and I want that to be behind me as well," said Hartland.

"It's spectaular, you feel all of the presence of the past bands there looking at you like 'is he going to make a good song?'"

Despite his developing music career, Hartland said he would not rule out more acting in the future, as he is "just trying things out".

While he has not yet had a chance to cover the iconic Gavin and Stacey theme song, Run by Stephen Fretwell, he said he would love to in the future.

"It's iconic," he said, adding "that would be brilliant".

articles.title: Hull adventurer Karl Bushby 'overwhelmed' at Humber Bridge crowds
articles.summary: The British adventurer is due to complete his 31,000-mile challenge in Hull on Monday.
articles.body:
British adventurer Karl Bushby crossed the Humber Bridge through thick mist on the final leg of his 31,000-mile (49,890 km), 28-year trek from South America to Hull.

Bushby left Chile in 1998 to head home to the UK without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until he had completed his journey, and not to use transport to advance.

The adventurer said he was "absolutely overwhelmed" by the crowds who lined the bridge.

Bushby, a former paratrooper, is due to complete the challenge on Monday and will be met by his mother, his son and granddaughter when he arrives in Hull.

The adventurer has said the opportunity to embark on his walk came after the breakdown of his marriage, when his wife returned to Northern Ireland with their son.

"When I left home and I walked down south first of all to test the machine that I first had, I don't remember any of that journey except for the Humber Bridge," he said on Sunday.

"There's that mystic look to it where you can't see the other side of the river.

"The Humber Bridge has always been that iconic landmark in my mind."

Aged 29, Bushby said he walked out of Punta Arenas, Chile, with a few hundred dollars in his pocket and turned north for home.

By the time he swum back across the English Channel on 5 October, Bushby, now 57, had crossed four continents, a frozen sea, deserts, mountains and jungles.

"[I'm] just absolutely overwhelmed," he said on Sunday when he spoke to BBC Radio Humberside .

By "we", Bushby may have meant the royal we, or The Beast, the cart he has spent 28 years pushing.

"This is my Wilson," he said, a reference to a volleyball that Tom Hanks's character talked to in the film Cast Away.

"I'm just a homeless guy pushing a shopping trolley, and the next thing you know is this," he said, nodding to the crowds lining the bridge.

"And I have to really kind of just stop and think about what this means to other people."

On Monday morning, Bushby will begin the final part of his walk back to his mother's home in north Hull.

He will set off from Hessle and walk to Queen Victoria Square, where a reception will be held for him outside the Civic Hall.

articles.summary: US First Lady Melania Trump on Sunday hailed a humanitarian operation in Ukraine’s Kherson region.

She said the ceasefire in the city of Oleshky should become a “starting point for lasting peace”. articles.title: Shootings near 3 college communities leave 1 dead, at least 21 injured
articles.summary: A violent Halloween across the U.S. leaves police investigating three shootings near college campuses in Indiana, Alabama and Delaware, while Dallas shootings leave four dead.
articles.body: Shootings in three college communities over the weekend left one person dead and at least 21 others injured. Indiana, Delaware and Alabama police are each investigating shootings in crowded parties near college communities, according to police and university statements. Seven were hospitalized in Bloomington, Indiana, near Indiana University's homecoming, while the University of Delaware is still counting victims (six are reportedly hospitalized) and the Magic City Classic football game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State near Legion Field in Birmingham, Alabama, left at least one dead and eight wounded. SHOOTING AFTER MAGIC CITY CLASSIC IN ALABAMA LEAVES 1 DEAD, 8 INJURED After midnight near Indiana University, officers monitoring a large crowd around Kirkwood Avenue and Dunn Street heard shots around 1:30 a.m. ET and saw a man with a firearm running from the area, Bloomington police said. Officers took the man into custody near Dunn Meadow, and recovered a gun and shell casings in the area. Police said it remains unclear whether the suspect fired any shots. No deaths were reported in Bloomington, and police said they did not know whether there were additional victims. FLORIDA A&M UNIVERSITY SHOOTING LEAVES 12 INJURED, INCLUDING 6 CHILDREN, NEAR FOOTBALL STADIUM A disturbance in the crowd may have preceded the shooting, police said. Indiana University police and Indiana State Police assisted in the response. In Newark, Delaware, a shooting on Saturday night rocked the University of Delaware. "We are deeply concerned about the shooting on Main Street Saturday night, which has impacted our entire community," the school's director of media relations Peter Bothum told Fox News Digital in a statement. "We are grateful to the Newark Police Department, which is leading the investigation. We will continue to communicate confirmed information, which will be shared on a dedicated alerts page (udel.edu/about/alerts) and updated as we learn more." University President Laura Carlson said victims were receiving care and thanked Newark police, campus police and other first responders for providing on-scene care. POLICE OFFICER, WOMAN SHOT NEAR NOTRE DAME AFTER FOOTBALL TAILGATES "I am writing to you about the shooting last night in Newark on Main Street, although it is difficult to know what to say when violence like this erupts in our community," she wrote in an email to the school community. "We are all impacted," she continued. "I ask that you keep the victims in your thoughts and hearts as they receive care. Please also recognize the impact and toll on our students and community members who were on Main Street last night and witnessed this violence." The university did not provide a confirmed number of victims or say whether anyone had died, but a report indicated at least six were hospitalized. The investigation is being led by Newark police. The school urged students and staff to follow its campus alerts page for confirmed updates. In Birmingham, Alabama, one person was killed and eight others were wounded Saturday night after the Magic City Classic football game near Legion Field, police said. Officers found nine people with gunshot wounds in the 400 block of Graymont Avenue West shortly after 7:50 p.m. ET. SEVERAL UNIVERSITY OF IOWA STUDENTS WOUNDED IN DOWNTOWN SHOOTING AFTER FIGHT ERUPTS NEAR CAMPUS One victim was in critical condition and seven others were stable, authorities said. Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue. He said he was "very grateful that more people weren’t injured." Police spokesperson De'Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters for questioning, and "multiple weapons" had been found and secured. Alabama State and Alabama A&M are historically Black universities and archrivals whose annual contest has been played for more than 100 years. Nearly 70,000 fans attended Saturday's game, won by Alabama A&M 31-28. The event draws some of the largest crowds in the country for games played in their college football division. POLICE MAKE ARREST AFTER GUNFIRE DURING CALIFORNIA HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME LEAVES 1 DEAD The Magic City Classic has such a deep history that Alabama State coach Eddie Robinson Jr., a former NFL linebacker and alumnus of the school, proposed creating a Hall of Fame for the game. SEARCH UNDERWAY FOR SUSPECTED GUNMAN OUTSIDE NOTRE DAME FOOTBALL GAME VS MICHIGAN STATE In addition to the shootings near campuses, police in Dallas say four people are dead and 15 are injured following three separate shootings in a Dallas neighborhood. Police Chief Daniel Comeaux said police are still trying to determine if the shootings were related or what led to them. Comeaux said some arrests were made, but he did not specify how many or what charges were involved. "This is a really big scene. It's spread out," Comeaux said. "We are interviewing some individuals right now that we have arrested, still trying to figure out exactly how it ties into all the shootings out here." No arrests have been made, police said in a news release. A preliminary investigation indicates an altercation preceded the shooting. articles.title: Sydney armed police start street patrols after Bondi Beach attack
articles.summary: The new police unit is a security measure in response to last year's deadly shooting attack at a Hanukkah festival.
articles.body:
Heavily-armed police officers have started patrolling Sydney's streets, as part of heightened security measures following last year's deadly shooting at Bondi Beach.

The Armed Response Command (ARC) will see specially trained officers in busy tourist areas carrying long-arm rifles – an unfamiliar sight for most residents.

New South Wales police say the officers will also patrol major events like sports matches and places of worship "to prevent, deter and rapidly respond to serious threats, including active armed offender incidents".

Fifteen people - including a 10-year-old girl – were killed in December when two gunmen opened fire on an event marking the Jewish festival of Hanukkah at the popular beach.

The attack was Australia's worst mass shooting in almost three decades and prompted sweeping gun law reforms and a crackdown on hate speech.

One resident told ABC news that the sight of armed police was "unnerving".

"They are just everywhere. Those guns are huge."

But another woman told the broadcaster that seeing police with weapons made her feel safe.

ARC is specifically designed to be "highly visible across Sydney, driving specialist vehicles and carrying rifles," New South Wales police said in a statement.

Its role "is built on a simple principle - preserving life," Detective Superintendent Andrew Evans said.

The shooting on 14 December put huge pressure on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government, with calls for immediate action on antisemitism.

Jewish communities have welcomed the new police operation, which will eventually consist of 250 officers, but others have called for safeguards to protect human rights.

"No Australian wants to see officers with military weapons on our streets, but the sight of body bags is far worse," Alex Ryvchin, co-CEO of Executive Council of Australian Jewry, said.

But Amnesty International Australia said it was concerned about the "militarisation of policing", and asked for assurances from the state government that ARC will not be used to suppress peaceful protests.

"Any expansion of police powers and capabilities must be accompanied by clear, publicly accessible rules, robust independent oversight and accountability," said the organisation's Andrew Witheford.

The New South Wales administration defended the new measures.

"Our world changed forever. That's just the truth of it, right across this country. And I said it at the time, we will never be the same again," the state's Police Minister Yasmin Catley told the ABC.

One of the alleged gunmen, Naveed Akram, has been charged with 78 offences including 15 counts of murder, 40 counts of attempted murder, and one count of committing a terrorist act.

His father, Sajid Akram, 50 - who was also armed and shot at the crowd on Bondi Beach - was killed by police at the scene.

articles.title: Democrat Haley Stevens endorses Republican in key Michigan Senate race
articles.summary: Haley Stevens, a former congresswomen who lost out on the Democratic nomination to Abdul El-Sayed, endorses his opponent days before the vote.
articles.body:
A Democrat in Michigan has endorsed the Republican candidate in the state's closely-fought US Senate contest, as a spat with her own party's candidate Abdul El-Sayed escalated just days before the vote.

Haley Stevens, a sitting congresswoman who lost out on the Democratic nomination to El-Sayed, made a surprise appearance alongside the Republican candidate Mike Rogers at a church on Sunday.

"I don't belong in Abdul's campaign," she said in a video posted to X shortly after that appearance. "Who we are as Michiganders is not hate and is not what we are getting out from our Democratic nominee right now."

"That's why I am endorsing Mike Rogers," Stevens said.

Stevens also said El-Sayed had told her she was no longer welcome in his campaign.

"This is a very close election, we all know that, but Abdul made clear that I was not welcome in his campaign, that he didn't need me there, that he didn't want me there," Stevens told reporters after the Sunday church service.

The pair had been scheduled to appear together at a different event on Sunday, but El-Sayed reportedly asked her not to come.

They had clashed publicly over a campaign advert from a liberal group which blamed Israel for high food prices.

El-Sayed criticised the advert and said he had nothing to do with its contents.

The Michigan Senate race is considered by analysts to be one of the tightest in Tuesday's midterm elections, which will decide which party controls Congress for the next two years.

It is one of a handful of battleground contests that will ultimately decide control of the Senate.

When asked about Stevens' endorsement, El-Sayed told reporters he was focused on problems Michiganders are facing.

"At the end of the day I don't think about Haley Stevens," he said. "None of this matters."

Rogers, meanwhile, welcomed Stevens' endorsement and said it showed "courage".

Many of her staff reportedly resigned after her announcement, while the chair of the Democratic Party in the state said Stevens' decision "shows that she has abandoned everything she claims to care about".

"We reject the attempts by Stevens and bad-faith actors to divide our party and undermine our momentum," Curtis Hertel said in a statement.

Over the weekend, as Stevens' criticism of El-Sayed escalated, a number of Democratic politicians in Michigan publicly encouraged her to end the feud and back the party's candidates.

"I have no idea what the hell Haley Stevens is doing," State Senator Mallory McMorrow told CNN.

On Sunday, Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer said he and the party were firmly behind El-Sayed, without directly mentioning Stevens.

"Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan," he said.

articles.title: In 1981, residents began raising funds to save an 1899 Utah schoolhouse bought for just $1, launching a 40-year effort that led to a nearly $2 million restoration and a new life as a community centre
articles.summary: In Spring City, Utah, an old brick schoolhouse has taken on a new purpose after decades of efforts to keep it standing.
articles.body: In Spring City, Utah, an old brick schoolhouse has taken on a new purpose after decades of efforts to keep it standing. Built in 1899, the Romanesque-style building once accommodated eight classrooms before closing its doors to pupils in 1957. It later faced the possibility of demolition, but local preservationists stepped in to secure the property. What followed was a lengthy campaign involving fundraising, public support and a substantial financial commitment from the town. National Trust for Historic Preservation reported, after restoration work costing nearly $2 million, the former school reopened in May as a community centre, giving the historic building a place in the town's present-day life.How a $1 purchase saved the historic Spring City schoolhouse from demolitionThe schoolhouse was built at a time when Spring City was developing its public institutions around the needs of a growing community. Its brick exterior and Romanesque architectural features gave it a distinctive appearance, while its eight classrooms provided space for local education. That role came to an end in 1957, when the school closed.The building did not immediately find another permanent use. It was subsequently used for storage, leaving its future uncertain. The Daughters of Utah Pioneers eventually purchased the property for just $1, with the intention of preventing its demolition. The symbolic purchase kept the structure from being lost, although securing the building was only the first step in a much longer preservation effort.Four decades of fundraising helped keep the restoration aliveEfforts to raise money for the schoolhouse began in 1981, when an annual fundraising event was established. The campaign continued over the years, reflecting the difficulties of financing a major restoration in a small community. Spring City has around 1,000 residents, making a project of this scale a considerable undertaking.The town became directly involved in securing the money needed to move the work forward in 2011. It obtained a loan and a grant to support the restoration, providing a more substantial financial foundation for the project. The process still required time, planning and coordination, as the building needed extensive attention before it could safely serve a public purpose again.Nearly $2 million spent restoring Spring City's historic schoolhouseThe restoration involved far more than cleaning up the old classrooms or repairing the exterior brickwork. Much of the interior required attention, including the original woodwork, wainscoting and staircase. Some features had to be restored, while others needed rebuilding to bring the structure back into usable condition.Modern building systems also had to be installed. The work included new drywall, heating, mechanical equipment and electrical infrastructure. These repairs were necessary to make the former school suitable for regular use, while preserving the character that made it worth saving in the first place.As reported by the National Trust for Historic Preservation, the project cost almost $2 million. For a town of Spring City's size, finding the resources to complete such extensive work required a sustained effort involving different groups and individuals over several decades.Former schoolhouse reopens as Spring City's community centreThe restored building reopened in May as a community centre, marking a change from its original educational purpose. Its new use allows residents to continue gathering in a property that has been part of the town's history since the end of the 19th century.The renovation retained the building's pioneer-era appearance, despite the amount of structural and technical work carried out inside. Its historic details remain part of the finished space, linking the new community facility with the people who originally built it.For Alison Anderson, president of Friends of Historic Spring City, the project also demonstrated what a small town can achieve through years of cooperation. She pointed to the importance of people working towards the same outcome without making recognition or personal credit the focus of their involvement.Preservation effort leaves a lasting connection to Spring City's pastAnderson said the restoration had given her a deeper appreciation of the craftsmanship involved in constructing the town's early buildings. The quality of the original work became particularly apparent during the process of repairing the woodwork, staircase and other historic features.The schoolhouse's survival was not the result of a single decision or fundraising campaign. Its story stretches from the Daughters of Utah Pioneers' $1 purchase to the town's financial involvement in 2011 and the years of restoration that followed. Each stage helped keep the building available for another generation.Its reopening as a community centre gives Spring City a practical use for a property that might otherwise have disappeared. After more than 40 years of preservation efforts, the former schoolhouse has returned to public life, no longer as a place for lessons, but as a shared space for the town.You use AI every day. articles.title: Gandhinagar: New rules mandate rapid reporting of sterilization-related deaths
articles.summary: Gujarat tightens accountability for sterilization deaths with 24-hour reporting, mandatory death audits, and revamped state/district Quality Assurance Committees.
articles.body: Gandhinagar: District health authorities in Gujarat will be subject to a stricter accountability framework for sterilization-related deaths, complications and failures, with the state govt mandating time-bound reporting, medical audits and corrective action under a revamped quality assurance system.Through a notification issued on Oct 15, govt has reconstituted state and district-level Quality Assurance Committees (QACs). Under the revised framework, district committees will be required to report major discrepancies in sterilization programmes and other healthcare delivery systems to the state panel. In the event of a sterilization-related death, district authorities must inform the state-level family planning indemnity subcommittee within 24 hours and conduct a mandatory death audit.The State Quality Assurance Committee (SQAC) will function as the apex policy-making body for quality assurance initiatives and will be responsible for overseeing their implementation, outcomes and shortcomings. Chaired by a senior official of the health and family welfare department, it will guide, monitor and review quality improvement efforts across districts.District committees will also be tasked with reviewing hospitalization cases arising from sterilization complications and failures, assessing service quality at govt and accredited private health facilities, and recommending corrective measures where standards are not met.The revised framework replaces earlier govt resolutions issued in 2007, 2008 and 2014. articles.title: Chennai may get moderate rain from Monday as Cyclone Murasu moves towards AP coast
articles.summary: Chennai likely to see cloudy skies and moderate to heavy rain Monday as Cyclone Murasu nears AP coast; IMD issues orange alert for Chennai, Tiruvallur.
articles.body: Chennai: Chennai is likely to remain cloudy and may receive heavy rainfall on Monday as Cyclone Murasu moves closer to the south Andhra Pradesh coast. Though the city is likely to escape the cyclone’s intense rainfall zone, its outer rain bands are expected to bring showers to Chennai and neighbouring districts from Monday morning, offering some relief from the prevailing warm conditions. For Tiruvallur and Chennai, IMD has forecast heavy rainfall on Monday and issued an orange alert.The cyclonic storm is expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by Monday morning before crossing the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur on Monday night. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the system moved west-northwestwards at 27kmph in the six hours preceding 2.30pm on Sunday. It was centred about 480km east-southeast of Chennai, 550km east-southeast of Nellore and 610km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam.For Chennai, the main impact is expected to be from the peripheral rain bands rather than the cyclone’s core. Tamil Nadu Weatherman Pradeep John said rain bands could extend towards north Tamil Nadu, including Chennai, from early Monday morning. The city is likely to witness cloudy skies, intermittent showers and cooler conditions as the system moves towards Andhra Pradesh.“Chennai may miss out on the heavy rainfall associated with the cyclone, but moderate cloud bands could still move across the city, bringing some spells of rain as the system passes,” he said. North Chennai, particularly coastal areas, could receive stronger spells, while the Ponneri-Gummidipoondi-Pulicat belt also has a chance of heavy rainfall, he added.The IMD has forecast light to moderate rain at many places in northern coastal Tamil Nadu on Monday and Tuesday with heavy rain at isolated places. Squally winds are also likely along and off the north Tamil Nadu and Puducherry coasts. Dry weather is expected to prevail across TN from Wednesday.Meanwhile, temperatures remained relatively high across Tamil Nadu on Sunday. Madurai recorded the state’s highest maximum temperature of 35°C. Chennai recorded 32.3°C at Meenambakkam and 33.2°C at Nungambakkam, both slightly above normal. Vellore recorded rainfall of 1.4 cm, while parts of Kancheepuram district received 1.2 cm rainfall on Sunday.Cyclone Murasu’s Tamil linkChennai: The cyclonic storm brewing over the Bay of Bengal has been named Murasu, after the traditional Tamil percussion instrument used in ancient times to make public announcements and convey important messages across villages and kingdoms. The name was proposed by India as part of the international cyclone-naming system.The name features in the list of 13 names submitted by India to the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) and United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) Panel on Tropical Cyclones in 2020. The list was prepared with contributions from 13 member countries, each submitting 13 names.India’s other contributions to the list include Gati, Tej, Aag, Vyom and Neer. articles.title: Dirty parks, defunct lights: Locals won’t celebrate Diwali if issues aren’t resolved in Greater Noida
articles.summary: Greater Noida Sector 3 residents warn they won’t celebrate Diwali unless GNIDA fixes streetlights, water supply issues, neglected parks and broken roads.
articles.body: Noida: Non-functional streetlights, water supply challenges, neglected parks and deficient civic infrastructure — residents of Sector 3, Pocket-A, have been piqued over the dire state of civic amenities in the neighbourhood for years. Vowing not to celebrate Diwali if concrete steps are not taken, they have written to the CEO of Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA), listing their grievances and calling for immediate action on pressing issues.In the letter, Sudhir Chaudhary, a resident of the area, articulated the struggles faced by the residents, highlighting that it has been nearly 15 years since they first moved to the area, yet they remain deprived of fundamental services that are essential for a reasonable quality of life.The residents’ concerns encompass several critical issues that have sparked frustration and discontent among the community. The letter seeks not only acknowledgement of the issues but also a commitment to timely resolutions, as residents demand timelines for addressing each concern, ensuring that they are kept informed throughout the process. A response from GNIDA is awaited on the issue.Some of the key areas of concern include the lack of adequate streetlights. The visibility on streets has drastically declined due to inadequate lighting, raising safety concerns for residents, especially at night. Some streetlights are described as “extremely dim,” while damaged electricity poles pose an acute risk of collapse. Residents urged immediate inspections and repairs to enhance safety and security in the area.Secondly, the parks within Sector 3 are facing severe maintenance issues. Overgrown grass and untrimmed hedges have made footpaths nearly impassable, while overflowing dustbins contribute to unhygienic conditions. Additionally, trees have not been pruned for over a year, Chaudhary said.Another critical issue includes water supply challenges. Chaudhary said that the residents have been grappling with inadequate water pressure, making it difficult to fill tanks on upper floors. Further, reports of contaminated water supply have raised alarm bells among residents, prompting calls for an immediate investigation into potential pipeline issues.Apart from that, deficient civil infrastructure adds to residents’ woes. “Many roads in the sector are in disrepair, posing dangers for vehicular and pedestrian traffic alike. The absence of commercial shops in the vicinity has made it increasingly difficult for residents to access essential goods, compelling them to seek supplies elsewhere. articles.title: From ‘satisfactory’ to ‘poor’, air quality slips in 48 hours
articles.summary: Noida, Greater Noida and Ghaziabad air quality worsened in 48 hours, with AQI rising to ‘poor’ (Noida 248); forecasts warn further decline.
articles.body: Noida: The region’s air quality deteriorated drastically over the past 48 hours, slipping from ‘satisfactory’ on Friday to ‘moderate’ on Saturday before plummeting to ‘poor’ across Noida and Ghaziabad on Sunday.Noida’s average air quality index (AQI) stood at 248, a sharp decline in quality from 106 the day before. Greater Noida and Ghaziabad followed this trend with AQI recorded at 228 and 227, against 120 and 110, respectively, on Saturday.Forecasts indicate that the air quality is slated to deteriorate further in the region as the mercury drops unless there is a fresh bout of northwesterly disruption in the weather system.Experts say ‘poor’ AQI conditions can cause breathing discomfort to people with lung diseases, asthma and heart diseases. Prolonged exposure to ‘very poor’ AQI can even lead to respiratory illness among healthy people.On Friday, some air quality monitoring stations in Noida and Ghaziabad recorded AQI in the ‘good’ range. By Sunday, however, some monitoring stations were starting to record air quality above the 300 mark – in the ‘very poor’ zone.Of the seven monitoring stations in Noida, Sector 39 and Sector 62, areas dominated by heavy traffic flow, recorded an AQI breaching the 300 mark. The remaining five areas had AQIs ranging from 200 to 269.In Greater Noida, the Knowledge Park III station was the only one that recorded a ‘moderate’ AQI, while the rest all recorded ‘poor’ air. In neighbouring Ghaziabad, two of the city’s eight stations – Loni and New Tehsil Loni – recorded ‘very poor’ AQI. Loni station’s AQI stood at 373 on Sunday, just 27 points under the ‘severe’ mark.Sunday morning saw the region packed with a steady fog, with dust pollution and vehicular emissions thick in the air.According to experts, following the massive unseasonal rainfall on Friday that acted as a natural scrubber, the cessation of rain and the transition to a clear sky on Sunday caused an immediate reversal in the region’s air quality.As daytime temperatures recovered to 29 degrees Celsius and wind speeds dropped below 15 kmph, the lower atmospheric boundary layer began to trap emissions once again. While the steady northwesterly winds helped prevent a catastrophic spike, the lack of active precipitation and the cooling evening temperatures (dropping to 18 degrees Celsius) reduced vertical mixing depth, allowing particulate matter to quickly accumulate and driving the regional AQI back up to the ‘poor’ category.With no immediate weather system in sight, the situation is likely to worsen in the days to come, forecasts showed.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Noida | Silver Rate in Noida | Bank Holidays in Noida | Public Holidays in Noida | Noida AQI | Weather in Noida | Petrol Price in Noida | Diesel Price in Noida | CNG Price in Noida | LPG Price in NoidaStay updated with the latest Noida news. articles.title: Four-lane bridges built to ease commute from Maduravoyal to Nolambur rendered ineffective as link road remains narrow, encroached
articles.summary: Chennai’s new four-lane bridges to Nolambur/Mogappair are hampered by a narrow, encroached Nolambur Union Road; widening and eviction actions pending.
articles.body: Chennai: Months after the city corporation opened two bridges along Poonamallee High Road to reduce travel time for people heading towards Nolambur or Mogappair, commuters lament that nothing much has changed -- thanks to encroachments and incomplete widening works that make travel an arduous task.The four-lane bridges over the Cooum redirect commuters from Poonamallee High Road onto Nolambur Union Road at Maduravoyal. Commuters headed to Nolambur/Mogappair can use this road instead of the Poonamallee High Road, cutting travel time by 10 minutes. “However, that plan has remained only on paper. In fact, taking the Poonamallee High Road itself is a better choice because the union road gets jammed during peak hours. The road is hardly two lanes wide and is uneven on several stretches. The corporation’s work to widen it has stalled midway,” said S Ravishankar, a resident of Nolambur.When TOI visited the spot, several huts and shops lined the road. articles.title: Odisha adds 7,800 new 5G home broadband users in Sept: Trai
articles.summary: Odisha added 7,871 5G FWA home broadband users in Sept 2026, raising total to 4.63 lakh; Jio leads with 3.66 lakh, Trai says.
articles.body: Bhubaneswar: Odisha has added over 7,000 new 5G Fixed Wireless Access (FWA) or home broadband users in Sept, taking the total number of subscribers to 4.63 lakh, up from 4.55 lakh in Aug, according to a report released by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) recently.The report, ‘Highlights of Telecom Subscription Data’ at the end of Sept 2026 indicated that the state has registered an additional 7,871 users during the month. Reliance Jio continued to dominate the segment with 3.66 lakh subscribers, accounting for nearly 80% of the market, while Bharti Airtel had over 96,000 users.The report also revealed that the number of mobile users who sought to switch telecom operators through mobile number portability (MNP) in the month remained high. The data showed that 2.93 lakh mobile subscribers in Odisha submitted requests to port their numbers during Sept.Telecom analyst Prasanta Sahu said the growth in fixed wireless broadband highlights increasing demand for high-speed internet beyond conventional fibre networks. "5G FWA is emerging as a practical alternative in locations where fibre connectivity is either unavailable or expensive to deploy," he said.Users, meanwhile, cited convenience and quick installation as key reasons for opting for the service. “I shifted to 5G broadband after facing delays in getting a fibre connection. The installation was completed within a day, and the speed has been satisfactory for work and streaming," said Swaroop Das, an IT professional in Bhubaneswar.Another user, Priyanka Mohanty, a postgraduate student, said that wireless broadband has improved connectivity in her locality. “Earlier, we had limited broadband choices. The new service offers stable internet without the hassle of cable-related disruptions," she said.Industry expert Subhransu Pattnaik said that operators are aggressively expanding FWA services in Tier-II cities and peripheral urban areas. “The technology is helping companies tap broadband demand faster without the delays associated with laying underground fibre. articles.title: Gujarat vessel destroyed in attack off Oman coast; 13 crew rescued
articles.summary: Indian-flagged MSV QUBA from Gujarat was destroyed in an aerial attack off Oman while sailing UAE-Somalia; all 13 crew rescued; owners seek probe, compensation.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: An Indian-flagged vessel carrying general cargo from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to Somalia was allegedly struck by an unidentified aerial weapon off the coast of Oman on Oct 29 and engulfed in a fire that destroyed it completely. All 13 Indian crew members were rescued, while the vessel’s owner and crew members from Gujarat have incurred substantial financial losses.In a representation submitted to the Union ministry of external affairs on Saturday, Kasam Jafrabadi, a resident of Mota Salaya in Mandvi, Kutch, called for a probe into the incident and compensation for the loss of the vessel, MSV QUBA (MNV 2183).The representation said the vessel belonged to Abdul Matin Maklai and was captained by Abdul Majid Tarmamad Karani. It was transporting general cargo from Shindagah International Port in the UAE to Bosaso Port in Somalia.The vessel left the UAE on Oct 28 at 9.08am UAE time. The alleged attack took place at about 4.30am UAE time the next day off the Oman coast.The strike sparked a blaze, which completely destroyed the vessel, the representation said.Jafrabadi, who is related to the vessel’s owner and captain, said the 13 crew members survived after fishermen rescued them.The representation expressed gratitude to the fishermen for their help, while drawing attention to the financial consequences of the incident for the vessel’s owner, captain, crew members and their families.“The vessel’s destruction has resulted in heavy financial losses and affected the livelihoods of its owner, captain, crew members and several families who depend on the vessel’s commercial operations,” the representation said.The family has asked the ministry of external affairs to intervene and coordinate with the Oman govt and maritime security agencies to ensure an impartial investigation. It has also called for the weapon used in the attack, as well as the individuals or organisations behind it, to be identified.The representation urged diplomatic action to safeguard Indian maritime interests and ensure the security of Indian nationals involved in international trade.It also called for an evaluation of the financial damage and compensation from those responsible, the countries concerned and insurance companies.The family has sought financial aid and rehabilitation assistance for the 13 crew members and their families, besides information about the investigation.Mandvi-Kutch MLA Aniruddha Dave had reached out to the affected families in Mota Salaya, expressed concern and assured them that a representation would be submitted to the authorities concerned, the letter said.The family has appealed to the Centre to fix legal responsibility and ensure that the probe proceeds beyond its preliminary findings.The representation said the incident was not just a financial setback but had also raised questions about the safety of Indian nationals and an Indian-flagged vessel on a lawful international voyage.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ahmedabad | Silver Rate in Ahmedabad | Bank Holidays in Ahmedabad | Public Holidays in Ahmedabad | Ahmedabad AQI | Weather in Ahmedabad | Petrol Price in Ahmedabad | Diesel Price in Ahmedabad | CNG Price in Ahmedabad | LPG Price in AhmedabadStay updated with the latest Ahmedabad news. articles.title: Michigan Dem Haley Stevens endorses Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers
articles.summary: US Rep Stevens lost Democratic primary to Abdul El-Sayed and now endorses his Republican opponent in the Senate race.
articles.body:
In a blow to Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign for the United States Senate in Michigan, his former primary opponent, US Representative Haley Stevens, has endorsed Republican candidate Mike Rogers.

Stevens stunned party officials on Sunday by appearing with Rogers at a Detroit church service as tensions between her and El-Sayed boiled over two days before the election that will determine the balance of power on Capitol Hill.

“I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the US Senate. Today, I do not belong to Abdul’s campaign,” she said in a video posted on X.

Stevens’ surprising support for US President Donald Trump’s endorsed candidate in the tightly contested race comes after she was uninvited to a joint event on the same day with El-Sayed, who defeated her by a slim margin in the August primary.

“Who we are as Michiganders is not hate, and [that] is not what we are getting out of our Democratic nominee right now,” Stevens said.
